background: UBS Group is Switzerland's only remaining global bank after absorbing Credit Suisse, the world's largest wealth manager, with Swiss retail and corporate banking, asset management and an investment bank, and a balance sheet far larger than the Swiss economy.
synthesis: Two of the three main agencies rate the group, A on average and A- at the weaker of them, both on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 14 Apr 2026. The ratios are solid in isolation, CET1 of 14.4% and leverage of 5.8% on the capital side, LCR of 177% and NSFR of 115% on liquidity, and none has moved materially over the past four periods (figures to 30 Jun 2026). The flagged news is heavy and points one way: the newest items, on 28 Sep 2026, are an analyst estimate of the profit cost of the latest Swiss capital plan and a US fine. The fine is a conduct cost; the capital plan is what a depositor should follow, since it means a stronger balance sheet bought with years of retained earnings.
